blocks.text: [III, 220] From these things it is clear that the sign expressed the thing signified exceedingly well; yet the reality rises many degrees above the figure. For the bronze serpent, although a symbol of God's grace, could of itself do nothing. For he who turned to it was healed not by the thing that he saw, but by you, the Saviour of all, as the author of the book of Wisdom XVI, 7 truly says. But Christ has life hidden in himself, Coloss. III, 3, and gives life to whomever he wills, Ioh. V, 21. The sight of the serpent brought healing to the Israelites alone; faith in Christ brings it to all, for in him there is neither Jew nor Greek, but you are all one in Christ Jesus, Gal. III, 28. The bronze serpent rescued those who looked at it from the death of the body in such a way that they still remained subject to death; through Christ we are freed for ever from the death of the soul as well as of the body, as he himself teaches, Ioh. XI, 26. Whoever lives and believes in me shall never die. The power of the bronze serpent lasted for a day or two; but Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today, and for ever, Hebr. XIII, 8. Therefore it was impious to worship the bronze serpent, and Hezekiah rightly broke in pieces so outstanding a monument of divine power when he noticed that the Israelites were burning incense to it, 2 Regum XVIII, 4. But all honour the Son, just as they honour the Father, Ioh. V, 23. And all the angels worship him, Hebr. I, 6. And God has highly exalted him, and given him a name which is above every name, that at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of things in heaven, on earth and under the earth, Phil. II, 9. 10. Accordingly, whereas the bronze serpent which the Israelites worshipped was broken in pieces, on the contrary those will be broken in pieces who refuse to Christ the worship due to him. Psal. II, 9. You shall break them with a rod of iron, and dash them in pieces like a potter's vessel. And Dan. II, 44, of the kingdom of Christ: It shall crush and consume all those kingdoms, but it shall itself stand for ever. And in the parable, Luc. XIX, 27: Those enemies of mine, who did not want me to reign over them, bring them here and slay them before me.
